summary.intent: Investigate why the web-e2e CI job was cancelled after merging phase 68.2, diagnose whether it was a regression, and fix the underlying problem so the suite reliably passes in CI.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed a week-long 20-minute CI timeout as a serial-suite scaling problem (not a 68.2 regression), parallelized web-e2e to 3 workers with CI-aware timeout floors, root-caused and fixed 3 real races (conflict-detection cleanup, rotation-durability SC#4 fail-closed gate, full-workflow instant-visibility asserts), fixme'd a genuine product gap (recovery.html v3 incompatibility) with a tracked todo, reached a reliable green run (212 passed/1 fixme, ~16 min), opened PR #593, and began resolving CodeRabbit/Greptile review feedback.

repo: Every substantive push to main since PR #578 (2026-06-29) had been cancelling web-e2e at the 20-minute CI cap; only trivial chore commits skipping the job via path filter looked green — this was mistaken for a phase-68.2 regression but was pre-existing.

web-e2e wallet accounts are minted via privateKeyToAccount(generatePrivateKey()) giving each test a unique address/userId/browser context by construction — no cross-test collision risk when enabling parallel workers.

23 of 24 web-e2e spec files already use test.describe.serial and provision their own accounts — this is exactly the granularity Playwright parallelizes when fullyParallel:false and workers>1 (whole files go to workers, intra-file order preserved).

Web3Auth Sapphire Devnet login is a real external DKG taking ~90s per login with no bypass (api-helpers.getAuthToken is an unimplemented TODO) — this was originally why the suite ran workers:1 ('avoid overwhelming Web3Auth'), but 4 concurrent DKGs proved to be a non-issue (zero login flake observed).
playwright-report upload step is gated `if: failure()`, which does NOT run when a job is cancelled (timeout) — this is why timed-out CI runs have zero artifacts to inspect.

Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on every /auth/refresh call; the app has an in-flight refreshPromise dedup guard (apps/web/src/lib/api/auth.ts:36-70) specifically to avoid concurrent-refresh 401s — test cleanup code that does a raw bypassing fetch doesn't get this protection and races.

deleteAccount cascades and removes all related DB records server-side (apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ex:225-245) — per-item UI-delete loops in test afterAll hooks are redundant and can blow hook timeouts under load.

apps/api ipns.service.ts resolveRecord prefers the DB-cached record whenever dbSeq >= networkSeq (anti-rollback protection) — this means stale-record replay tests against a mock relay can never reach the client if the DB row is already ahead, requiring test-side floor injection instead of relay replay to exercise the client's fail-closed gate.

recovery.html (standalone disaster-recovery tool) is hardcoded to the retired v2 single-key vault blob format and pre-#578 folder envelope; the SDK has hard-cut to v3 two-key blobs + node/v3 sealed codec — the shipped recovery tool currently cannot recover any current-format vault. This is a genuine, tracked product gap, not a test/CI issue.

ciFloor()-style helpers (enforce a minimum wait under CI while honoring longer explicit timeouts) are an effective pattern for eliminating whack-a-mole timeout tuning across many hardcoded per-call-site waits.

code.finding: workers set to process.env.CI ? 3 : 1 (settled after 4-worker trial caused login/multi-delete contention); fullyParallel kept false to preserve describe.serial ordering; test timeout raised to CI ? 90_000 : 30_000 to absorb parallel-load slowness.

ciFloor() helper enforces a 60s minimum wait for waitForItemToAppear/waitForItemToDisappear under CI regardless of caller-supplied shorter timeouts, catching ~65 call sites with serial-calibrated 10-30s waits; later patched to preserve explicit timeout:0 (Playwright 'no timeout') instead of flooring it, per CodeRabbit review.
BLOB_V2_VERSION=0x02 hardcoded; detectBlobVersion only recognizes v2, so v3 blobs (byte 0x03) trigger 'not v2 format' error at line ~1160 before recovery Step 2 ever renders.
deserializeVaultBlobV3 is the reference implementation recovery.html needs to mirror to parse current-format vault blobs.

resolveRecord's dbSeq >= networkSeq branch returns the cached DB record, shadowing any stale replayed network record — this is the reason rotation-durability's stale-record replay test can't work via mock-relay replay and needed a durable-floor injection instead.

deleteAccountViaPage issued a raw fetch('/auth/refresh') bypassing the app's refresh dedup guard, racing concurrent app-initiated refreshes and getting 401 on the single-use token — fixed with retry-with-backoff.

afterAll reordered to call deleteAccountViaPage first (cascades server-side) and dropped the redundant per-item UI-delete loop that was blowing the 60s hook timeout under parallel load; orphaned confirmDialog var/import also removed.

SC#4 test fixed with test.setTimeout raised 60s→240s plus a new writeDurableSeqFloor helper that injects a seq floor directly into IndexedDB to genuinely trigger the client-side enforceResolved fail-closed rejection (real mutation, no product code touched, no stubbing of the security gate).

Instant isItemVisible assert immediately after a move raced the UI refresh; fixed by converting to wait-backed expectItemPresent/expectItemGone helpers, then globally applied via guarded script across ~58 similar instant-assert call sites in the file to avoid repeated whack-a-mole CI cycles.

workflow: Estimating serial-suite progress from application server logs (e.g. counting wallet logins/IPNS publishes) is a useful proxy when the CI job was killed before any report artifact uploaded.

Reading Playwright HTML-reporter error-context.md DOM snapshots at the moment of failure is decisive for distinguishing 'slow but correct' (item present in DOM, just after the assertion timeout) from 'genuinely broken' failures — avoids guessing from stack traces alone.

When multiple failures recur identically across different worker counts (4 vs 3), that determinism is itself diagnostic signal that the failures are NOT contention/flake but deterministic pre-existing bugs merely exposed by running further into the suite.

Dispatching parallel investigative subagents on disjoint files (one per suspected root cause) let 3 independent fixes proceed concurrently without working-tree collisions, resuming with SendMessage/context preserved for the most complex one (rotation SC#4).
`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh run view ...` calls were repeatedly rejected as malformed tool calls requiring retry — some friction in the gh CLI invocation pattern within this harness.

friction: GitHub Actions doesn't expose live logs mid-run via API — had to wait for job completion to inspect progress, slowing the iterative tuning loop.
HTML-only CI reporter means no per-test pass/fail lines in stdout; failure details had to be extracted by grepping/tailing raw logs each time.
A compound git push+dispatch command timed out on a slow pre-push hook, causing a duplicate CI run dispatch that had to be manually cancelled to save runner minutes.
`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh run view` tool calls were rejected as malformed multiple times, requiring immediate retry with a differently-formed call.

Iterative timeout/worker tuning produced repeated whack-a-mole: fixing one failure let the suite progress further and exposed the next deeper failure in the same long describe.serial journey, requiring several full CI round-trips (~10-16 min each) to converge.
Hit the session token/usage limit mid-task ('You've hit your session limit'), requiring the user to say 'please continue'.
A Prettier formatting violation was introduced by an edit and had to be caught by lint and reformatted before commit.
open_items: recovery.html v3 port (parse v3 vault blob header + rewrite recoverFolder for node/v3 sealed envelope) — tracked via enriched GSD todo .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-03-port-recovery-tool-to-v3-vault-format.md; recovery.spec.ts:68 left as test.fixme pending this port.
multi-account-wallet.ts:77 login timeout (90s) is contention-sensitive under parallel workers; flagged as the lever to bump if Web3Auth login flake resurfaces at 3 workers.

PR #593 review resolution in progress: 3 CodeRabbit nitpicks (timeout passthrough on expectItemPresent/expectItemGone, redundant double-wait collapse, ciFloor timeout:0 preservation) applied; 2 Greptile threads (recovery fixme, conflict cleanup fallback) to be replied to and resolved as by-design/not-applicable.
Repo convention confirmed: opening a PR can trigger a bot chore(release) commit, requiring git fetch+rebase (never force-push) before any further pushes to the branch.
